Ideological confusion, spiritual restlessness, and a general difficulty telling breakthrough from delusion all belong here.
uranus-trine-neptune: The trine lets radical change and collective imagination move together easily across a long stretch of years. New forms find ready belief, and belief finds new forms without either forcing the other. It is among the least abrasive configurations two outer planets can make, and correspondingly hard to point at. Its work is a slow shift in what a culture finds thinkable.
uranus-opposition-neptune: The opposition falls some eighty-five years after the conjunction, and brings the impulse to break free face to face with the impulse to dissolve. An age's revolutionary claim and its spiritual longing stand fully articulated on opposite sides, each having become the thing the other must answer. Given the length of the cycle, this is a generational condition rather than a passing one, and it is lived through rather than resolved.
uranus-conjunction-pluto: Uranus and Pluto meet about every one hundred and thirty years, in 1965 and 1966 most recently, and the pairing fuses revolt with irreversible power. The conjunction opens a cycle of radical restructuring: what breaks now does not get put back, and the movements that begin under it tend to carry both genuine liberation and real ruthlessness without being able to separate them. It is one of the most consequential signatures in mundane astrology, and among the least frequent.
uranus-sextile-pluto: The sextile makes deep change available without forcing it. Reform can reach the foundations rather than the surface, and power can be redistributed without the confrontation such redistribution usually requires. Because both bodies are slow, the phase runs for years and works by accumulation. What it alters is generally not noticed until someone compares the beginning of the period with the end of it.
uranus-square-pluto: The square is the cycle's crisis, and the 2012 to 2015 passage is the recent case: uprisings, institutional distrust, and confrontations between entrenched power and the demand to break it, sustained over years rather than weeks. Neither side can absorb the other, and neither withdraws. The phase is genuinely turbulent and it is not random; it marks where a structure and the pressure against it have both grown too strong to coexist quietly.
uranus-trine-pluto: The trine lets rupture and transformation cooperate over a long span. Deep change proceeds without the violence that usually accompanies it, and the reorganisation of power meets no proportionate resistance. The ease is real and worth reading carefully: what consolidates unopposed under this phase is as likely to be a concentration as a liberation, and the period supplies no friction to tell them apart.
uranus-opposition-pluto: The opposition brings the long cycle to its culmination, with the impulse to break free and the power that does not yield fully visible across the sky. Whatever began at the conjunction has reached the point of open confrontation on a historical scale. Because the two move so slowly, this is a condition of an era, and its characteristic feature is that both sides regard the conflict as fundamental rather than negotiable.
uranus-conjunction-node: Uranus crossing the eclipse axis, an infrequent contact given how slowly both points move. Rupture meets the place of interruption, and the two reinforce each other: a break in the collective direction arriving at the point where such breaks are marked. It works over months and several passes.
uranus-conjunction-chiron: Uranus and Chiron meet only about every one hundred and twenty-six years, and myth already pairs them: Chiron gave up his immortality so that Prometheus could go free. Sudden change meets the wound, and the exchange is the point. What opens here tends to involve a break that costs somebody something real, and a liberation that is paid for rather than seized. Cycles this long describe conditions rather than episodes.
uranus-sextile-chiron: The sextile lets awakening and injury inform each other without strain. New methods of treatment, teaching or repair find room, and the people who know a problem from the inside get an unusually clear hearing. It is a permissive rather than a forcing phase, and its results tend to be practical: the way something painful is handled quietly changes and does not change back.
uranus-square-chiron: The square sets the demand for freedom against an unhealed injury. Change arrives faster than the damage can absorb, or the wound refuses the liberation on offer because it has learned not to trust one. Both readings describe the same friction. The phase is disruptive in a specifically raw way, and what it exposes is where a break would reopen something rather than resolve it.
uranus-trine-chiron: The trine allows sudden insight and long-carried pain to work together. Relief arrives from an unexpected direction, and understanding earned the hard way finds a new form to travel in. It is one of the gentler outer-planet contacts, and its effects are individual and cumulative rather than historic.
uranus-opposition-chiron: The opposition sets rupture against the wound across the whole width of a very long cycle. The break and the cost of the break stand facing each other, fully articulated. Periods under it tend to produce arguments in which liberation and harm are both real and cannot be traded off, which is uncomfortable and accurate.
neptune-conjunction-pluto: Neptune and Pluto meet about once every four hundred and ninety years, last in 1891 and 1892, which places their conjunction outside ordinary reckoning altogether. Dissolution fuses with irreversible transformation, and the cycle it opens is civilisational: the deep imaginative substrate of an age is remade. On any human timescale this is background rather than event, and it is read for what it makes possible over centuries.
neptune-sextile-pluto: Neptune and Pluto have held a sextile for most of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries, an unusually long alignment produced by the eccentricity of Pluto's orbit, and astrologers from Rudhyar onward have treated it as a standing condition of the modern era rather than a passing aspect. Vision and transformative power have been continuously available to each other. It explains very little about any particular week and a good deal about the period as a whole.
neptune-square-pluto: A square between Neptune and Pluto falls roughly a century and a quarter after their conjunction and lasts for years. The dissolving of collective belief grinds against the deep restructuring of power, and the two undermine rather than answer each other. It is not a configuration any living observer has worked with directly, and it is read as an epochal strain rather than as a situation anyone manages.
neptune-trine-pluto: A trine between these two runs for years and describes a long harmony between imaginative life and transformative power, in which the deep changes an age is undergoing are matched by its capacity to picture them. Because both bodies are so slow, this is a climate rather than a condition anyone acts within. Its effects register as the character of a period.
neptune-opposition-pluto: The opposition falls some two hundred and forty-five years after the conjunction, and sets the dissolving of an age's certainties against the power that is remaking it. This is the widest stretch of the slowest cycle in ordinary astrological use. Nothing about it operates on the scale of a decision; it names a condition that historians rather than participants are placed to describe.
neptune-conjunction-node: Neptune crossing the eclipse axis, rare and slow. Dissolution meets the point of interruption, which reads as a collective direction losing definition rather than being redirected. The contact spans a year or more and describes an atmosphere rather than an event.
neptune-conjunction-chiron: Neptune and Chiron meet about every seventy-three years, and the pairing puts the wound into the water. Suffering becomes collective, atmospheric and hard to locate: not one injury but a shared sense that something is wrong, expressed in art, faith and general unease rather than in identifiable grievance. The conjunction opens a cycle in which pain and transcendence are difficult to distinguish, which is the source of both its compassion and its confusion.
neptune-sextile-chiron: The sextile allows compassion and injury to meet productively. Care extends more readily to what cannot be fixed, and artistic or spiritual work made out of difficulty finds an audience that recognises it. The phase asks nothing and offers a good deal. What it does best is make suffering less isolating without pretending to resolve it.
neptune-square-chiron: The square blurs the wound rather than clarifying it. Genuine injury and vague malaise become hard to tell apart, remedies attract belief out of proportion to their evidence, and the wish to transcend the pain competes with the work of tending it. Escapism is the characteristic error of the phase, and it is sympathetic rather than foolish: the pain being avoided is real.
neptune-trine-chiron: The trine lets dissolution soften what will not close. Compassion, art and devotion do their ordinary work of making pain bearable, and the boundary between an injury and the rest of a life becomes less absolute. Nothing is cured here. What changes is how much room the wound is required to occupy.
neptune-opposition-chiron: The opposition sets the longing to dissolve against the injury that refuses to dissolve. Whatever comfort the cycle promised at its conjunction now stands opposite the thing it failed to reach. The phase tends to produce a hard-edged disenchantment with consoling answers, which is painful and is also the point at which real care becomes possible.
pluto-conjunction-node: Pluto crossing the eclipse axis, one of the least frequent contacts in ordinary practice. Irreversible power meets the point where the pattern breaks, and the reading is of a change of collective direction that will not be reversed once made. It holds for years across several passes.
pluto-conjunction-chiron: Pluto and Chiron meet about every sixty-three years, and myth stages their meeting directly: Chiron, unable to die and unable to heal, chose to go down to Hades so that Prometheus could be released. Irreversible power meets consented suffering. The conjunction opens a cycle about damage that cannot be undone and has to be inhabited instead, at the scale of communities rather than individuals.
pluto-sextile-chiron: The sextile makes depth available to the work of repair. Buried injury can be brought up and examined without the process becoming a crisis, and what surfaces can be used rather than merely survived. The phase supports investigation, testimony and the slow business of turning harm into something a community knows about itself.
pluto-square-chiron: The square forces the wound and the power that caused it into contact. What was buried resurfaces with enough force to compel attention, and the friction is between a demand for acknowledgement and a structure invested in not giving it. The phase is harsh and clarifying in equal measure. Nothing about it is optional once it starts.
pluto-trine-chiron: The trine lets transformative power and long-carried injury work together without a struggle. Deep change proceeds through what was damaged rather than around it, and hard experience turns into a source of real authority. The configuration is quietly powerful and easily missed, since it produces competence rather than crisis.
pluto-opposition-chiron: The opposition brings the cycle to its culmination, with irreversible power facing the injury it left. The period tends to produce reckonings that are fully public and fully unresolved: the harm is undeniable, the power is intact, and neither can be argued out of existence. What the phase supplies is an accurate view of both.
chiron-conjunction-node: Chiron crossing the eclipse axis. The wound meets the point of interruption, and what surfaces tends to be an old collective injury arriving exactly where the direction is being reset. It holds for months and repeats, which is generally when the material becomes usable rather than merely painful.
